page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v5 belongs to the memory-optimized Eads v5 family and operates on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Compute resources are provided by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 128 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Cache hierarchy details include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, while vector execution includes standard AVX without AVX-512 support.

Storage consists of 644 GB of bundled local SSD storage suitable for swap, cache, and temporary workloads. The instance does not include GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance reveals strong single-core CPU throughput and top-tier PassMark memory scores. Cached memory bandwidth achieves 1033.28 GB/s on small blocks. In contrast, uncached 256 MB memory transfers demonstrate a hardware tradeoff, registering lower read and write throughput of 38.7 GB/s and 22.85 GB/s. Static web serving reaches 17.7 GB/s and Redis SET operations deliver 15.84 million operations per second, placing aggregate multi-core throughput in the average benchmark tier.

With its dense 8:1 memory-to-core configuration and integrated local SSD capacity, the instance offers balanced resource efficiency for memory-heavy setups without incurring the overhead of unused accelerator hardware. The server is well suited for hosting relational database engines, Redis and Memcached caching systems, real-time analytics, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and 128 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Integrated storage is provided via a 644 GB local SSD, while GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are absent. Hardware acceleration includes AES, VAES, and SHA instructions, alongside base AVX support. Performance benchmarks reflect strong single-core processing and high PassMark memory scores, though uncached large-block memory bandwidth remains lower relative to peer architectures. Multi-core metrics, caching operations, and static throughput align with median hardware tiers. The configuration offers cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks requiring local scratch storage, making it well suited for enterprise database management, in-memory caches, ETL data processing, and large business applications.
